input.question: How can there be a maximum speed if there is no absolute frame of reference in space?
input.ground_truth: > I could travel at a constant speed, choose myself as the frame of reference and claim that I'm standing still. Now, suppose I first accelerate to the speed of 0.99c, then establish my current fixed speed as the speed 0. Wouldn't I then be able to continue to accelerate, eventually past c? Yes. You can. The difference however is that, in relation to an observer "standing still", time is passing slower for you, your length is contracted etc. So, in relation to this observer you won't be able to reach *c*. However, in your perspective, you really will be able to reach your destination faster if you keep accelerating as if relativity didn't exist. The thing is that you will reach your destination faster because as you accelerate, time slows down for you, so in a blink of an eye, you're in the other side of the universe (depending on how much you accelerated from 0.99c)

Okay! Let’s imagine you and your friend are both on skateboards, and you’re both rolling really fast in different directions. Now, if you look at your friend from your own skateboard, it might look like they’re moving a little bit slower than if someone standing on the ground (like your mom) was watching both of you.

Now, scientists say that there’s a fastest speed anything can go in the universe: it’s called the speed of light. But you might wonder, “How can there be a fastest speed if there’s no special spot in space to measure from?” Like, if everyone is moving differently, how do we know what the ‘maximum’ really is?

Here’s the simple answer:  
No matter how fast you or your friend are moving, if you both check how fast light goes (like a flashlight beam), you’ll both see it moving at the same super-fast speed! That speed is the “maximum” because nothing, not even a rocket or a superhero, can catch up to light. This rule is the same for everyone, no matter how they’re moving. That’s why we can have a maximum speed—even if there’s no special “standing still” spot in space. It’s like everyone agrees on how fast light goes, no matter where they are or how they’re moving!
